title: Restore principle pointers and close the slice 3 leftovers
action: Every port note that dropped a pstack principle pointer because its bee principle did not exist yet: now that slices 4's principles exist, put the pointer back as the bee slug (bee-principle-<slug>) in the playbook or skill it came from, and mark it restored in the note. Then close the leftovers in reports ppb-24c and ppb-25c: worktree-cleanup names bee-arena; multi-phase-plan owners never rebase (decision b25486e3) and it names the read role for gathers; note or restore the feature port's rebase wording and the 'the app is small' rebuttal; move the misplaced restored note in session-ppb-12.md; note the table-only rows ppb-11c marked not noted. Write docs/history/pstack-playbook-port/port-notes/principle-pointers.md listing each pointer restored. No line names Cursor, Graphite, bugbot or poteto-agent; no hand-picked model or subagent_type; tools become bee counterparts per D2. Copy the pstack LICENSE verbatim to each new skill directory as LICENSE.pstack. Run bee dev regen and commit the rendered trees and the manifest with the cell. Facts you need, so no lookup is required: an advisor or design runner goes out as `bee dispatch prepare --runtime claude --kind advisor --role <role> --json`; a judge or reviewer as `--kind reviewer`; read-only gathers as `--kind gather`; the blind-lane roles are lane-1, lane-2 and lane-3, and `bee blind check` checks a blind brief; write these spellings into the skill text, never run them. Bee commands you may run in this cell: cargo test, `.bee/bin/bee dev regen`, `.bee/bin/bee dev release-manifest --check`, `.bee/bin/bee knowledge check`, and `bee herding notify`. Never run `bee dispatch` or any of its `--help`; the worker guard refuses it and the cell stops. A principle or skill that does not exist in skills/ yet keeps its method as a plain sentence and is named in the port notes.
